items.title: Asian Rice Price Climbs Near Two-Year High in Inflation Threat
points: (Bloomberg) -- A benchmark Asian rice price climbed to the highest in almost two years, threatening to accelerate food inflation as the El Niño weather pattern disrupts production of the staple grain.
Farmers across much of Asia are in the midst of harvesting the grain, and drier-than-usual weather has proven a hurdle for crops in growers like India, the world’s leading exporter.

That’s pushing prices higher, with 5% broken white rice from Thailand — another major shipper — rising to $499 a ton as of Wednesday, the highest since December 2024, according to the Thai Rice Exporters Association.
Rough rice futures in Chicago are also up more than 80% since the start of the year.
The El Niño weather phenomenon underway is one of the most powerful on record and linked to drier conditions across much of South and Southeast Asia, where more than half the world’s rice is grown.

items.title: Sustainable aviation fuel may cost 2-3 times more than conventional jet fuel: Centre’s draft policy
points: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) could cost at least two to three times as much as conventional jet fuel, according to a draft policy by the Centre, which proposes financial incentives to encourage its production as India prepares to introduce blending…
Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is an alternative fuel made from non-petroleum feedstocks that reduces air pollution from air transportation, according to the US Department of Energy.
The draft proposes a phased blending mandate for international aviation, requiring fuel suppliers to ensure a 1% SAF blend in 2027, 2% in 2028, 3% in 2029 and 5% in 2030.

items.title: ECI separates online Form 6, accompanying declaration for States undergoing SIR
points: A View of the Logo of the Election Commission of India at the Nirvachan Sadan.

Moorthy The Election Commission of India (ECI) has separated the Form 6, used for fresh voter registration, and an accompanying declaration in its online version in States where the SIR exercise is underway.
Earlier in September, it had already withdrawn the declaration from its digital platforms in States where SIR had been completed.
Form 6 is used for fresh voters registrations and since the SIR in Bihar a separate declaration had been added with it in physical forms.
However, in the digital mode, it was a single form and this included the declaration.
The ECI had justified it saying a single OTP for the two documents had led to suggestions that the form had been tweaked without the approval of the Union Law Ministry.
This change in the online version of the Form 6 had been one of the issues flagged in dissent notes by the two Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

items.title: Korea to Introduce Cornerstone Lockups to Curb Post-IPO Selloffs
points: South Korea’s top financial regulator will introduce a system for cornerstone investors in initial public offerings to curb sharp price drops after listings.

The Financial Services Commission said institutions that commit to lockups of at least six months will be allowed share allocation in advance under the new system, which got government approval Tuesday.
For example, the 32% plunge of data center infrastructure company Elice Inc. ’s shares on their first day became a signal for the global neocloud business.
IPOs in Korea have largely disappointed investors this year, with the shares of companies that listed in 2026 down a weighted-average 32%, far behind the Kospi’s gain of 38%.
SK Hynix Inc. scrapped plans for a potential $10 billion US listing of its Solidigm unit after regulators and shareholders objected that it could dilute minority investors.
Half of an investor’s allocation would be locked up for six months, 30% for eight months and the remaining 20% for 10 months, according to the FSC.

items.title: Digital traffic simulation model, road safety audit for 2,205km of Delhi roads
points: Under spotlight for congestion on Delhi’s arterial road network and worsening traffic congestion, the Public Works Department (PWD) has decided to undertake a comprehensive traffic simulation study and road safety audit covering 2,205.68km of roads across…
The ₹11.17-crore exercise will use digital models to study traffic movement on individual road stretches and test possible solutions to congestion before implementing them on the ground.
The study, which is expected to be completed within three months, will cover 1,796 roads across the three zones.
These include 270 roads spanning 426.28 km in the South Zone, 1,137 roads covering 1,374.76 km in the North Zone, and 389 roads stretching across 404.64 km in the East Zone.
PWD oversees arterial road networks with width more than 60ft while smaller roads are overseen by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi.

items.title: RSS to be expanded into 88 regional units: Dattatreya Hosabale
points: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) will restructure its organisation into 88 divisions, replacing its existing 46 regional units, as part of its centenary-year expansion plans, general secretary Dattatreya Hosabale said on Wednesday, claiming a 150%…

Speaking on the concluding day of the Sangh’s three-day annual meeting at Daly College in Madhya Pradesh’s Indore, Hosabale said the restructuring would help the organisation plan and coordinate its activities more effectively across the country.
“Till now, we had 46 prants (regional units).
Following organisational elections in November-December, presidents (Sanghchalaks) and new executive bodies will be elected, and 88 sambhags (divisions) will be formed.
Future work plans will be prepared from the perspective of these 88 divisions”.
Highlighting the organisation’s expansion, Hosabale said the number of shakhas in West Bengal had increased by 150% over the past year.
Weekly programmes have started at 48 locations in Arunachal Pradesh, while two shakhas are now functioning in Mizoram.

items.title: Resume DPR preparation for elevated highway on Edappally–Aroor NH bypass: Hibi Eden tells NHAI
points: Ernakulam MP Hibi Eden met National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) Chairman Santosh Kumar Yadav and sought his intervention for the immediate resumption of work to ready a detailed project report (DPR) for an elevated highway that the NHAI had mulled…

The NHAI ought to ready the alignment, design, cost and implementation strategy on a priority basis, so that the four-lane corridor does not remain a bottleneck when the rest of NH 66 is widened to six-lane.
An elevated highway in the corridor is in the larger public interest of not just Kochi but the entire State, he said in a letter addressed to the NHAI Chairman.
The letter and the meeting assume significance since the NHAI has prioritised the proposed 50-km Kochi Outer Ring Road (ORR) over the elevated highway.
“The ORR cannot replace the Edappally–Vyttila–Aroor NH 66 bypass that carries substantial traffic originating from, destined for, or connecting Kochi city.
The two projects can, therefore, serve complementary rather than substitutive functions,” the letter said.

items.title: Kerala High Court denies bail to student accused of circulating morphed images of fellow students and teachers
points: The Kerala High Court has denied bail to a student accused of circulating obscene morphed images of fellow students and teachers, observing that the allegation against the petitioner was serious and prima facie indicated a premeditated criminal act on his…

Justice Kauser Edappagath noted that the petitioner was the owner of two social media accounts through which the photographs of female students were shared and offered for sale along with the purported obscene video content.
The investigation had also revealed that the payments were collected through the UPI account linked to him, and that his social media accounts also held obscene and child pornographic content.
The petitioner had argued that there was no evidence linking him to the alleged offences, and that the grounds of arrest were not communicated during his arrest.
However, the records reflected that the grounds were communicated to him and his relatives, the court observed.

items.title: Case registered over bomb hoax at Kochi airport
points: The Nedumbassery police have launched a probe into an alleged bomb threat received by the Cochin International Airport.

The threat call, which turned out to be a hoax, was received at the airport’s official number around 11 p.m. on Tuesday, according to the first information report registered by the police on Wednesday.
The unidentified caller claimed that a bomb had been planted at the airport, triggering panic among employees and passengers.
The police registered the case on a complaint by a terminal manager at the airport.
The case was booked under Section 351 (criminal intimidation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 120(o) of the Kerala Police Act (causing a communication nuisance to any person).

items.title: Sebi eases KYC norms for NRIs, OCIs and foreign nationals, allows digital onboarding from overseas
points: Securities and Exchange Board of India has relaxed Know Your Client requirements for overseas investors.
This change enables non-resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India, and foreign nationals to onboard digitally.
Individuals from FATF-compliant countries can now submit KYC details remotely without being in India.
Intermediaries are allowed to rely on existing KYC records and conduct video verifications when necessary.
